title: No guard preventing nudgePaymentToken == NFTStaker.rewardToken (phUSD); misconfiguration siphons staker rewards into nudges
rootCause: The contract enforces `nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken` at line 121-126. It does NOT enforce `nudgePaymentToken != rewardToken`, where `rewardToken` is the NFTStaker's emission asset (phUSD in the production wiring). The asymmetry of guards is the root cause: one collision is forbidden, the structurally analogous one is allowed.
consolidatedDescription:
In single-dispatcher production wiring, `paymentToken == phUSD == rewardToken`, so the existing equality guard incidentally also blocks `nudgePaymentToken == phUSD`. The protection is a side effect, not a design.

In any multi-dispatcher deployment where one dispatcher uses a non-phUSD prime token, `paymentToken == USDC` and the existing distinctness guard then ALLOWS `nudgePaymentToken == phUSD`. The recommended hardening is to pass NFTStaker's rewardToken as an immutable to BatchNFTMinter at construction and reject collisions in the setter.
exploitScenarioCanonical: Not applicable at the production wiring. The existing distinctness guard incidentally protects against the rewardToken collision because paymentToken == rewardToken == phUSD in single-dispatcher mode.
unionOfMitigations: In `setNudgePaymentToken`, add a forbidden-tokens check. Pass NFTStaker's `rewardToken` into BatchNFTMinter at construction (immutable) and revert in the setter if `newToken` equals it.
Maintain an owner-configurable forbidden-tokens list for additional protocol-internal tokens.
Document explicitly in NatSpec that the nudge token MUST be a token the protocol does not consume elsewhere (an external incentive token).
preservedDetails: ECON-011 has the multi-dispatcher misconfiguration scenario.

sanitization.rationale: In the documented production wiring (single dispatcher, paymentToken == phUSD == rewardToken), the existing nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken guard incidentally protects against the rewardToken collision - so the finding has no impact on the actually-deployed configuration. The 'misconfigured BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook recipient' worst-case is a 'reckless admin mistake' pattern and is C4 known-invalid. The 'multi-dispatcher with non-phUSD prime token' scenario is forward-looking speculation about future code, which is also discouraged per project guidelines.
sanitization.surviving_scope: Add forbidden-tokens guard (immutable rewardToken passed at construction) as cheap defensive hardening (QA).

classification.justification: QA-grade defensive hardening recommendation. At the production wiring (single dispatcher, paymentToken == rewardToken == phUSD), the existing `nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken` guard incidentally protects against the rewardToken collision - no impact on the deployed configuration. The multi-dispatcher scenario is speculation about future code; the BalancerPoolerMintDebtHook misconfiguration is a reckless-admin-mistake pattern (C4 known-invalid). The fix (immutable rewardToken passed at construction + setter check) is cheap and worth recording.
preconditions: A future deployment in multi-dispatcher mode with at least one non-phUSD prime token AND nudgePaymentToken set to phUSD.
guardrails_observed: Existing `nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken` guard at lines 121-126 incidentally protects single-dispatcher production wiring.
Production wiring is documented as single-dispatcher in CLAUDE.md.
